Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class MetalThemeManager

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.MetalThemeManager
public final class MetalThemeManager extends Object
Chooses, creates and persists the Swing Metal theme the conventional 2D desktop is skinned with.

The 2D shell starts on the platform look-and-feel (GTK/Synth on Linux). Metal themes only affect the Metal look-and-feel, so applying one here switches the shell onto Metal (if it is not already) with the chosen palette, then refreshes every open window so the change is immediate. The selection and any user-created themes are persisted through DesktopConfig, and applyStored() re-applies the saved theme at desktop start-up - a no-op while no theme has been chosen, so the desktop keeps its native look until the user picks one in the control center.

The pure palette work lives in MetalThemeSpec (unit-tested headless); this class is the thin, EDT-bound live-application layer.

  • Method Details

    • builtIns

      public static List<MetalThemeSpec> builtIns()
      The built-in themes, in display order: Steel and Ocean (the stock JDK Metal palettes), Graphite (neutral slate-grey), Emerald (forest-green accent), Sunset (warm amber/coral accent), Glassy (an ice-blue palette that reproduces the native 3D desktop's translucent window-glass look - see MetalThemeSpec.GLASSY for the colour provenance), Midnight (deep navy), Rosewood (reddish-brown) and Sand (warm beige).

    • available

      public static List<MetalThemeSpec> available()
      Every selectable theme: the built-ins followed by the user-created themes decoded from DesktopConfig. Names are unique enough for the UI; a custom theme shadowing a built-in name still resolves to the custom one because resolve(String) searches customs first.

    • customThemes

      public static List<MetalThemeSpec> customThemes()
      The persisted user-created themes (never null).

    • resolve

      public static MetalThemeSpec resolve(String name)
      Finds a theme by name, preferring user-created themes over built-ins. Returns null when no theme carries that name.

    • toTheme

      public static CustomMetalTheme toTheme(MetalThemeSpec spec)
      Wraps spec in the live CustomMetalTheme Metal installs.

    • accentColor

      public static Color accentColor()
      The accent colour the 2D desktop is themed with: the explicit theme.accent the user picked in the control center, or - when none is set - the primary2 shade of the active Metal theme (falling back to Steel when no theme is chosen). Consumed by the window-decoration styling so the title bar tracks the theme. Never null.

    • apply

      public static void apply(MetalThemeSpec spec)
      Applies spec to the running desktop and persists the choice. Switches the shell onto Metal if needed, installs the palette and refreshes every open window. Safe from any thread; the look-and-feel work runs on the EDT. A null spec is ignored.

    • applySystem

      public static void applySystem()
      Reverts the 2D desktop to the native platform look-and-feel (GTK/Synth on Linux) that the shell starts on, undoing any applied Metal theme. Clears the persisted selection so the next start-up keeps the native look too (applyStored() is then a no-op), and refreshes every open window. Safe from any thread; the look-and-feel work runs on the EDT.

    • applyStored

      public static void applyStored()
      Re-applies the persisted theme, if one was chosen. Called from the 2D shell's reapplyConfig(); a no-op while the stored theme name is blank (the default), so the desktop keeps its native look until the user selects a Metal theme. Skips the refresh when that theme is already live.

    • addCustom

      public static MetalThemeSpec addCustom(MetalThemeSpec spec)
      Persists spec as a new user-created theme (replacing any existing custom theme of the same name) without changing the live look. Returns the stored spec.

    • removeCustom

      public static boolean removeCustom(String name)
      Removes the user-created theme named name (built-ins cannot be removed). When the removed theme was the selected one, the selection is cleared so the next start-up falls back to the native look. Returns true when a theme was removed.
